name: Panta OEM Diagnostics Expansion 6
usage_note: Curated from public OEM technical material archived by NHTSA. Verify exact engine, emissions level, VIN, calibration and current OEM procedure before repair.

documents.title: Detroit SPN 157 FMI 18 — fuel rail pressure high diagnostic logic
documents.source: NHTSA archived Detroit Diesel procedure SPN 157/FMI 18 GHG17 (2017)
documents.summary: Detroit's GHG17 SPN 157/FMI 18 procedure describes a high fuel-rail-pressure deviation condition. The MCM sets the fault when actual rail pressure remains substantially above requested pressure under the specified enabling conditions, with a reported 25 percent derate. OEM diagnostic flow starts by checking additional codes, then performing the Fuel System Integrity Check. The procedure evaluates key-on engine-off rail pressure and bleed-down, compares actual versus desired rail pressure during FSIC, and inspects the fuel-rail-pressure-sensor and MCM connector for corrosion. In the documented branch, excessive actual-versus-desired pressure can point toward the quantity control valve. Diagnostic lesson: use measured actual/desired rail pressure and the OEM test sequence instead of replacing the rail-pressure sensor solely because the code names fuel pressure.

documents.title: PACCAR MX-13 EPA2013 loose injector vs high-pressure fuel line leak — E091
documents.authority: PACCAR OEM Technical Information Bulletin E091
documents.source: NHTSA archived PACCAR/Peterbilt bulletin E091, June 2014
documents.summary: PACCAR bulletin E091 applies to MX-13 EPA2013 engines when fuel is leaking from high-pressure fuel lines or injectors. PACCAR notes that loose-injector and loose-high-pressure-line failures can present similar indicators and provides a decision flow to distinguish them. Diagnostic lesson: on an EPA2013 MX-13 with a high-pressure fuel leak or related fault, do not assume the visible leak source proves the root cause; use the OEM decision process and inspect the injector/high-pressure-line relationship before repair.

documents.title: PACCAR MX-11/MX-13 EPA2021 fuel-filter service contamination warning
documents.source: NHTSA archived Peterbilt Powertrain Service Bulletin, October 2023
documents.summary: A Peterbilt powertrain bulletin for EPA2021-compliant MX-11/MX-13 engines warns that incorrect fuel-filter draining or replacement procedures can introduce debris or contaminants into the high-pressure fuel system, producing drivability symptoms and fuel-system faults. Diagnostic lesson: when an EPA2021 MX engine develops fuel-pressure or drivability complaints after filter service, include recent service contamination in the history and inspection rather than immediately condemning high-pressure components.

documents.title: Cummins X15 CM2450 X142B inactive faults 14354/14356 — OEM multiplex messages
documents.authority: Cummins OEM Technical Service Bulletin TSB240097
documents.source: NHTSA archived Cummins TSB240097, revised May 2025
documents.summary: Cummins TSB240097 addresses inactive aftertreatment regeneration inhibit/force switch fault codes 14354 and 14356 on X15 CM2450 X142B. Cummins states that some OEM VECU multiplexing devices can send incorrect data-link messages that create high inactive-code counts, including during key-off events. The bulletin directs checking ECM calibration revision; later calibrations contain a fix for the check-engine-light behavior and Cummins specifically says not to replace the ECM or engine wiring harness for this issue. Diagnostic lesson: distinguish an OEM multiplex/calibration issue from an engine-harness or ECM failure before replacing hardware.
